newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B index up at noon on selective buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B index up at noon on selective buying.

text.p: Shenzhen's foreign currency B share market edged up at midday on Wednesday on selective buying of local issues with the index expected to move in a narrow range in the afternoon, brokers said.
The B share index added 0.43 points or 0.27 percent to 159.77 on turnover of HK$24.8 million.

The A share market rose 3.01 points or 0.64 percent to 472.91 on an extended rebound which began on Monday, following recent government anti-speculation measures that caused sharp losses, brokers said. Turnover was 3.7 billion yuan.

"Investors bought Shenzhen-based shares in anticipation that they will benefit from the Hong Kong handover, which will lead to closer economic ties between the two cities," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
The British colony of Hong Kong, which borders Shenzhen, reverts to Beijing's sovereignty at midnight on June 30.
"The Hong Kong stock market's recent bullish performance also boosted Shenzhen's B share market," the Guotai analyst said.
Shenzhen-based Chiwan Wharf Holdings Ltd was the best B share performer, rising HK$0.40 or 8.06 percent to HK$5.36.
On the A share market, Xibei Bearing Co was the sharpest gainer, surging 10 percent to its limit-up at 11.40 yuan.
